rationale:
bugs_open/420 (slug: order_intake_publishes_the_billing_email_as_the_sites_public_contact_and_registers_it_as_a_renderable_claim — the number is ambiguous, there is an unrelated 420 about the negation gate's prose walker).

One column, sites.email, carries two different facts with different consent. It is where the PLATFORM REACHES THE CUSTOMER (billing/delivery), and it is the address THE SITE PUBLISHES — the footer Contact block and the contact components assemble from it. Nothing in the schema, the seed or the chrome distinguishes them. On the first paid build (boxingonline.com, order BR-9AUZ59) seedCustomerIdentity wrote the payer's address to sites.email at build release and the site published it as a mailto on all 13 deployed pages plus 4 further occurrences on /contact.html. The owner saw his own personal address on a public site and ordered it off. It was his only because he was customer zero; on order 2 it is a stranger's. A billing address is not consent to publish.

The subtler half is that the register LICENSES RE-PUBLICATION. The same seeding minted an evidence_base fact 'Enquiries reach <payer>.' (id 'contact', kind 'entity', customer_attested). That is a RENDERABLE registered claim: section planning assigns fact ids to sections, writers write from facts, and validate_page_content would rightly PASS a page publishing it. So deleting the address from the column and the pages does not make it stay gone. This is not hypothetical — it FIRED on order 1, established by elimination [MEASURED 2026-08-31]: the build-briefing agent reads specs with aspect 'all', and the briefing spec it wrote twelve minutes after seeding carried contact.contact_email = the payer address, while the identity spec's contact block was all-null and the customer's brief text did not contain the address (direction->>'objective' ILIKE '%designconsultancy%' is false, 855 chars). The seeded register fact was the only possible source. A registered claim propagated into a second regeneration source inside one build.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-31, given to this session for the CLASS (the pre-existing ruling was per-site): when a customer pays but is never explicitly asked what contact details the site should show, the site publishes NONE. The payer's address is used only to deliver.

The fix applies the 2026-08-02 ruling literally. Publication authority becomes an OPT-IN direction key, published_contact, whose unsafe side (publish) is OFF by default. The payer's address is confined to stores no publish path reads — build_queue.direction.customer_email, where the collector already puts it and where the delivery dispatch already takes it from. NO SCHEMA CHANGE and NO BACKFILL: the delivery-contact store already exists, and adding a sites.delivery_email column would put a second contact-ish column on the very table every render path loads, guarded only by a comment — which is exactly what the 2026-08-02 ruling says does not survive a tree this many sessions share.

CENSUS, dated, because the delivery lane asked that every reader be found before the contract is split [MEASURED 2026-08-31]: 4 writers and 14 readers of sites.email. Writers: seedCustomerIdentity (the defect); sync_site_identity_action (fill-only-if-empty, wired into 0 live agents — dormant); update_site_content's sync_columns arm (fill-only-if-empty, 3 live agents); and the admin PATCH endpoint (site_admin_handlers.go:363-367, unconditional, the deliberate operator override — this one was missing from the bug file). The two spec-copying writers need no edit: on a customer build those stores receive the address ONLY via the seed's own writes, so closing the seed closes them at their source, and editing them would change estate behaviour this bug does not own.

A correction the census forced: the claim that the delivery chain reads sites.email is CONVENTION, NOT CODE. send_delivery_email_action takes customer_email as REQUIRED input_data supplied at dispatch (the 651 binding); no code in the send action or platform/delivery reads the column [MEASURED 2026-08-31]. That makes the split cheap — a recipe update, not a chain change. Likewise component_library.go:1989 is already gated on ctx.Email != "" (the bugs_open/111 gate); the defect is the VALUE, not a missing gate.

Two edits remove an info@<domain> synthesis (section_editor_actions.go and multipage_actions.go). Without them the default is hollow: post-fix the column is legitimately empty on customer sites, and these paths would publish a fabricated address that nobody owns and no mailbox answers, presented as the business's own choice. They are flagged severable if the council disagrees.

One consequence is worth stating because it is a guard obtained for free: validate_page_content loads sites.email as 'officialEmail' and passes any page publishing exactly that address. Post-fix the column no longer holds the payer address, so any residual occurrence of it on a page is FLAGGED by the existing hallucinated-email check instead of licensed — fix candidate 3's flag without a flag.

No data migration is needed and this is verified, not assumed: the seed ran exactly once fleet-wide, order 2 has not happened, and 0 current site_specs rows carry the address. Consumers named and told per the 2026-07-29 ruling: the site_delivery_and_editor lane (filed this bug, owns the delivery seam and the boxingonline pre-delivery list, has handed me the class fix and asked to be named on the delivery-recipe edit), the boxingonline.com session (its data is untouched by this change), and the check_contact_form_undeliverable path, whose arm shifts on unconsented sites from auto-publishing a mailto to needs_human_review.

plan.summary: Separate the two contracts sharing sites.email. The payer's address becomes delivery-only and is never written to any store a publish path reads; the published contact comes only from an opt-in direction.published_contact key whose unsafe side is OFF by default, so absent an explicit customer answer the site publishes none. The evidence-register fact that licensed re-publication is minted only from the consented address. No schema change, no backfill.

edits.rationale: Both doors, in one function. The sites UPDATE keeps its exact shape and its fill-only-if-empty guard; ONLY the $2 binding changes, from the payer email to the consented publishEmail. The contact evidence fact is minted only when publishEmail is non-empty. When nothing publishable was consented to, the function writes nothing at all and logs why. None of the council-settled boundaries from trail 7e3dd082 is undone: fires-only-on-intake-fields, never-overwrites-non-empty and never-supersedes-an-existing-register all survive verbatim — the change is to WHAT may be seeded, never to when or how. The header gains a fourth boundary saying so, and stating that 'sites.email IS the canonical identity store' still holds but sharpened: it is the canonical store of the PUBLISHED contact, and a billing address was never identity data — it is order data whose store already exists.

The producer half: boxBriefOrder gains an optional PublishedContact map mirroring the box's wire shape, and the direction literal copies it ONLY when non-empty — so an absent answer stays absent rather than becoming an empty object a downstream reader could mistake for one. This literal is where a reviewer of the PRODUCER sees the publish decision being made, which is the point of the 2026-08-02 opt-in shape as against a comment saying callers must be careful. Inert until the intake chat (on the box, not this repo) starts sending the key — the platform half ships first, defaulting to publish-nothing, which is the safe side and matches the owner's ruling.

Remove the info@<domain> synthesis. Post-fix an empty email column is the CORRECT and common state on customer sites, and synthesising here would publish a fabricated address nobody owns — making 'the site publishes no contact' quietly false. Absence renders as absence: the contact blocks are already gated on a non-empty email (bugs_open/111). Blast radius is 4 estate sites that currently display a fake string, at their next page-component rerender; chrome output is byte-identical because the chrome path never synthesised, so no ChromeRenderInputsVersion bump. Severable if the council prefers to keep it.

The same synthesis on the full-page build path. Removed for the same reason and in the same commit, because leaving one of the two would make the default true on some pages and false on others — the hardest kind of residual to notice.

These tests PINNED THE DEFECT: they asserted the payer email lands in sites.email and is minted as an 'Enquiries reach' fact. Rewritten to the new contract, with the negative assertion made load-bearing — argContaining gains an `absent` list, because a test that only checks what IS in the payload cannot see a leak, and 'the payer's address is not here' is the whole claim. Six mutations listed in the header; each was applied ALONE and broke its named test (run 2026-08-31), including rebinding $2 back to the payer email and re-minting the contact fact from it.

grounded_in: bugs_open/420: 'A billing address is not consent to publish.'
bugs_open/420: 'An address you must not publish cannot be represented as a publishable fact anywhere in the spec stack.'
seed_build_queue_action.go header (council trail 7e3dd082): 'sites.email/company_name IS the canonical identity store, not a fourth one' — preserved and sharpened, not undone.

[MEASURED 2026-08-31, by elimination] the briefing spec written 12:33:38 carried contact.contact_email = the payer address; the identity spec's contact block was all-null and the brief prose did not contain it; the build-briefing agent reads specs with aspect 'all'. The seeded register fact was the only possible source.

[MEASURED 2026-08-31] No code in send_delivery_email_action.go or platform/delivery reads sites.email; customer_email is REQUIRED input_data supplied at dispatch (651 binding). The 'delivery reads the column' claim is convention, not code.
[MEASURED 2026-08-31] 4 writers / 14 readers of sites.email, including the previously-unlisted admin PATCH writer at site_admin_handlers.go:363-367.
component_library.go:1988-1989 — the contact block is already gated on ctx.Email != "" (bugs_open/111); the defect is the value, not the gate.
validate_page_content.go:1718 loadSiteContactEmail loads sites.email as officialEmail and checkEmails passes any page publishing it — the licence, which post-fix becomes an active guard.

CLAUDE.md, OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 §2: 'New authority on a shared seam ships as an OPT-IN FIELD, not a documented contract... make X a field with the unsafe default OFF... A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.'

OWNER RULING 2026-08-31, this session, for the class: absent an explicit answer to 'what contact details should the site show?', the site publishes none and the payer's address is used only to deliver.
plan.risks:
The Go half is INERT until the next chassis build and roll. Until it rolls there is a live re-injury vector: boxingonline's build_queue row still holds direction.customer_email at status 'seeded', and re-seeding is the canonical build retry (bugs_open/326), so the now-NULL sites.email would be REFILLED with the payer address by the fill-only-if-empty guard. Do not re-seed that site before the fix rolls. The register survives re-seeding (WHERE NOT EXISTS); the column does not.

Edits 3 and 4 (removing the info@<domain> synthesis) change what 4 existing estate sites display at their next page-component rerender — they lose a fabricated address. That is a decision, not a surprise, and it is flagged severable. Chrome output is unaffected (the chrome path never synthesised), so no ChromeRenderInputsVersion bump.

check_contact_form_undeliverable's remediation arm shifts on unconsented customer sites: instead of auto-publishing a mailto to the column it will take the no-email arm (needs_human_review). Correct under the safe default, and named here so it is not later re-filed as a regression.

check_component_standards will report unconsented customer sites as 'missing metadata' (no email). Benign noise, named so it is not mistaken for a defect.

The published_contact wire shape ({email, phone, ...}) must be agreed with the box's intake-chat lane; that repo could not be inspected from here. The platform half consumes only .email today and ignores unknown keys, so the shape can widen without another platform change.

[UNVERIFIED] Whether the chat's customer_name field guarantees a BUSINESS name rather than a personal one. If personal, the same publish-without-consent shape exists for company_name at lower severity — business_name is minted as a fact and rendered. Flagged for the owner rather than fixed here, because the answer lives in the box repo.

This change does NOT cover the bug file's addendum half (rerender-pages with refresh_site_components:true refreshing head and header but SKIPPING footer). That is a rerender-mechanics defect in data propagation, orthogonal to which data is licensed to exist; the delivery lane owns it and is splitting it into its own file.
